title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Pattern Machine. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pattern Machine
options.thesis: The vocal chain as a hardware groovebox's encoder field: knob clusters per module, pad selectors, one display line that answers the control under your hand.
options.viewport: The chain canvas becomes the instrument face: mic in and out as silkscreened jacks, each effect a knob section, the touched knob's exact value on one LCD line.
options.risk: Grid-instrument density can outrun a non-engineer's confidence, and rotary drag must feel excellent or knobs read cheaper than faders.

raised.raise: Modules carry physical mass: weighted slabs with cut faces, never floating panels.
One unambiguous disabled texture and literal label honesty — every control called exactly what it is.
Palette economy: the accent is the only bright thing on the chassis; one blink marks the live control.
The touched module lifts a hair while its neighbors recede — focus theater at operator scale.

options.label: The Pedalboard
options.thesis: The chain as a pedalboard: one pedal per effect, knob-per-function, LED status, jacks implying the signal path down the board.
options.viewport: A pedalboard column: mic in at the top jack, pedals stacked in chain order, each with its knob cluster and a dry-marker name tape.
options.risk: The most familiar FX-on-the-web reference — familiar and effective, but a portfolio viewer has seen pedal UIs; committing flat-print, never photoreal.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: The console as a one-bit desktop: each effect a window with a title bar, dithered tone steps, marching-ants reorder ghosts.
options.viewport: Module windows on a dithered ground: checkmark menus for key and scale, meters as dithered bars, selections inverted.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — windows map to cards and desk affordances are universal; loses identification: a desk OS is not the venue's world.
options.risk: Retro pastiche dates a portfolio fast, and dithered tones fight meter precision.

options.label: Teletext Broadcast
options.thesis: The show as a broadcast index: the chain a numbered page of block-mosaic module rows, help waiting behind REVEAL.
options.viewport: A P100-style page: MIC IN header row, chain as numbered module rows, the OUT meter a mosaic bar, presets as three-digit page numbers.
options.case: Karaoke's own screen lineage — CD+G descends from it, so identification holds; loses clarity: knobs do not exist in a sixel world.
options.risk: The cell grid makes every control text; continuous sweeps and meters suffer.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Effects as cut blocks of weather assembled into transient architecture.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no karaoke or live-sound resonance, and dissolving architecture fights a show that must not break.
options.kept: Physical mass — modules as weighted slabs with cut faces.

options.label: Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone labeled with its literal quoted name; hazard diagonals for the disabled.
options.case: Stockroom culture is not venue culture; the bright ground fights a dark-stage eye.
options.kept: State coding with one unwavering grammar and literal label honesty.

options.label: Four Greens
options.thesis: The whole console in four greens, one tile grid, one blinking cursor.
options.case: Four shades cannot carry ten family colors plus meters without losing redundant encoding.
options.kept: Palette economy and the single blinking focus mark.

options.label: Poster Wall
options.thesis: Effects as poster tiles that expand on focus and reveal their controls.
options.case: Browsing theater is the opposite of an operate console; hidden-until-focus fights mid-show glanceability.
options.kept: The quiet focus lift — one card rises while neighbors recede.

canonCard.label: The standard web-audio console
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A tidy dark console any audio web app would recognize, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
